question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's position as paramount leader remains highly stable through 2026, underpinned by more than a decade of power consolidation, the 2018 removal of presidential term limits, and sustained anti-corruption purges that have sidelined potential rivals across the Politburo, Central Committee, and Central Military Commission. Recent personnel changes and the August 2026 Beidaihe conclave have reinforced loyalty networks without surfacing organized opposition or a designated successor. The 21st National Congress, scheduled for late 2027, is widely viewed as the venue for Xi's expected fourth term, with turnover focused on lower ranks under informal age norms rather than top-level transition. Trader consensus reflects the absence of credible near-term removal triggers. Low-probability disruptions could include acute health developments or unprecedented elite backlash, though neither is indicated by current patterns.
